newsitem.title: USA: CME weighs halving Eurodlr futures tick to $12.50.
newsitem.headline: CME weighs halving Eurodlr futures tick to $12.50.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange is weighing cutting in half the minimum price change for all Eurodollar futures months to keep business flowing in the pits when volatility dries up, CME brokers said Tuesday.

CME chairman Jack Sandner, president Rick Kilcollin and governor Scott Gordon met with Eurodollar brokers and traders in a special meeting Monday. "A number of issues were discussed but nothing was decided, a CME spokesman said.
Currently, eurodollar futures are quoted in basis points, or increments of 0.01 each worth $25.00. Under the plan, the minimum tick size would drop to 0.005 worth $12.50 each.
The half-tick approach is not entirely new in the eurodollar pit. CME began quoting the expiring January 1997 eurodollar and LIBOR futures contracts in half-ticks on January 2.
It since has made that policy permanent so that all expiring eurodollar and LIBOR contract months will be quoted in half-ticks during delivery month only, the spokesman said.
CME could decide to begin phasing in the smaller tick size for all contract months starting in February, said one broker.
"That was the gist of the meeting yesterday," the broker said. "It's not going to happen all at once."
The CME might decide to phase in the smaller tick size two contract months at a time to give time to educate the pit community to using different hand signals, he added.
Whether the change would keep business in the futures pit and away from over-the-counter markets remains debatable.
"Obviously in fast markets it's probably irrelevant, but when there's no volatility, some people think that's going to foster trade," the broker added.

"Half-ticks aren't going to create business," said another broker. "All it is is micromanaging a macro problem -- and the macro problem is that we don't have any volatility." ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
